record.title: Bosek's asymptotic harmonious coloring conjecture for hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $k,\Delta\geq 2$. A **harmonious coloring** of a $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is a vertex coloring that is rainbow on every edge and assigns distinct color sets to distinct edges; let $h(H)$ be the least number of colors in such a coloring. If $H$ has $m$ edges and maximum degree $\Delta$, then **Bosek's conjecture.** There exists a constant $c=c(k,\Delta)$ such that

$$
h(H)\leq \sqrt[k]{k!m}+c.
$$

The lower bound $\binom{r}{k}\leq m$ for a harmonious coloring using $r$ colors gives the leading-order term $\sqrt[k]{k!m}$, so the conjecture asks whether the known upper bound can be sharpened to this term up to an additive constant depending only on $k$ and $\Delta$.
record.source_name: Sebastian Czerwiński, “On harmonious coloring of hypergraphs”, arXiv:2301.00302 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.00302

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: The cubic-scale diameter conjecture for 4-configuration graphs
record.statement:
Let $D(n,k)$ denote the maximum diameter of a connected component of the $k$-configuration graph over all graphs on $n$ vertices. The $k$-configuration graph $\mathcal{R}_k(G)$ has independent $k$-sets of $G$ as vertices, with adjacency when one token is moved along an edge while preserving independence.

**Cubic-scale diameter conjecture.**

$$
D(n,4)=n^{3-o(1)}.
$$

The paper notes that the lower and upper bounds are not known to almost match for larger $k$; in particular, it is open whether the 4-configuration graph can have super-quadratic diameter, while the known upper bound is $o(n^3)$.
record.source_name: Nicolas Bousquet, Bastien Durain, Théo Pierron and Stéphan Thomassé, “Extremal Independent Set Reconfiguration”, arXiv:2301.02020 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.02020

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: The ball number bound for nontrivial nonsplittable links
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a link. Its **ball number** $\mathrm{ball}(L)$ is the minimum number of spheres needed to construct a necklace representation of $L$, and its **crossing number** $\mathrm{cr}(L)$ is the minimal number of crossings among all diagrams of $L$. A link is **nontrivial** if it is not the trivial link and **nonsplittable** if its components cannot be separated by a sphere.

**Ball number conjecture.** For any nontrivial and nonsplittable link $L$,

$$
\mathrm{ball}(L)\leq 4\mathrm{cr}(L).
$$

Moreover, equality holds if $L$ is alternating.

The proposed bound would improve the previously stated linear upper bound $\mathrm{ball}(L)\leq 5\mathrm{cr}(L)$. The source does not provide evidence that the bound or the equality statement has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Jorge L. Ramírez Alfonsín and Iván Rasskin, “Links in orthoplicial Apollonian packings”, arXiv:2301.03089 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.03089

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: Maximum-average-degree conjecture for non-2-mixing oriented graphs
record.statement: Let an oriented graph be a digraph with no pair of oppositely directed parallel arcs, and let its maximum average degree be the maximum of $2|A(H)|/|V(H)|$ over all non-empty subdigraphs $H$. A digraph is **2-mixing** if any two of its 2-dicolourings can be connected by single-vertex recolourings through 2-dicolourings. **Oriented-graph density conjecture.** Every non-2-mixing oriented graph has maximum average degree at least $4$. This is supported in the paper by proving the claim for 2-freezable oriented graphs; the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Nicolas Bousquet, Frédéric Havet, Nicolas Nisse, Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta and Amadeus Reinald, “Digraph redicolouring”, arXiv:2301.03417 (2023).
record.references:

record.title: The seven-hole conjecture for reduced clique graphs
record.statement:
A **chordal graph** is a graph with no induced cycle of length at least four. For a graph $G$, let $C_R(G)$ denote its reduced clique graph, whose vertices represent the maximal cliques of $G$ with adjacency defined by nonempty intersection after reduction.

**Seven-hole conjecture.** There is no chordal graph $G$ such that $C_R(G)$ contains an induced cycle with seven or more vertices.

Reduced clique graphs can have induced cycles of length six, so the conjecture asserts that seven is the largest possible length. It is presented as an open problem; no resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: Dillon Mayhew and Andrew Probert, “Reduced clique graphs: a correction to "Chordal graphs and their clique graphs"”, arXiv:2301.03781 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.03781

record.title: The minimal-zero conjecture for finite p-groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $p$-group of order $p^n$. Define

$$
\operatorname{mz}(p^n)=\min\{\operatorname{mz}(G)\mid |G|=p^n\},
$$

where $\operatorname{mz}(G)$ is the minimum number of elements of $G$ on which a non-linear irreducible character of $G$ vanishes.

**Minimal-zero conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{mz}(p^n)=\operatorname{mz}(G)
$$

if and only if $G$ has maximal class with an abelian maximal normal subgroup.

The conjecture is motivated by the proof of the lower bound and by computer calculations, and the source leaves it open for general $p$ and $n$.
record.source_name: Alexander Moretó and Gabriel Navarro, “p-groups and zeros of characters”, arXiv:2301.03917 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.03917

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: The dominating-set reformulation of the half-minimum-degree conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, with vertex set $V(G)$, minimum degree $\delta(G)$, open neighborhoods $N(u)$, and a set called **dominating** when it meets or is adjacent to every vertex of $G$.

**Dominating-set reformulation.** If

$$
\delta(G)\geq \frac{1}{2}|V(G)|,
$$

then there are vertices $u$ and $v$ in $G$ such that

$$
\{u,v\}\cup\left(N(u)\cap N(v)\right)
$$

is a dominating set.

The source presents this as a reformulation of the preceding restricted-pebbling conjecture, using the fact that graphs with minimum degree at least half their order have diameter at most two and invoking earlier results. It is therefore not an independent mathematical claim, but a domination-theoretic equivalent formulation.
record.source_name: László F. Papp, “Restricted optimal pebbling is NP-hard”, arXiv:2301.09867 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.09867

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: Exponential induced size-Ramsey conjecture for odd cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $\hat{r}^k_{\operatorname{ind}}(C_n)$ denote the smallest number of edges in a graph whose every $k$-coloring contains a monochromatic copy of $C_n$ as an induced subgraph. **Exponential induced-cycle conjecture.** For odd $n$,

$$
\hat{r}^k_{\operatorname{ind}}(C_n)\leq e^{O(k)}n.
$$

The paper proves the weaker bound $\hat{r}^k_{\operatorname{ind}}(C_n)\leq e^{O(k\log k)}n$ for odd cycles, so the conjectured exponential dependence on $k$ remains open.
record.source_name: Domagoj Bradač, Nemanja Draganić and Benny Sudakov, “Effective bounds for induced size-Ramsey numbers of cycles”, arXiv:2301.10160 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10160

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2023). “As an interesting open problem, we conjecture that an exponential bound in $k$ is also sufficient in the induced case.”

record.title: Johnston, Palmer and Sarkar's rainbow Turán conjecture for paths
record.statement:
Let $P_k$ denote a path on $k$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{ex}^{*}(n,P_k)$ be the maximum number of edges in a properly edge-colored $n$-vertex graph containing no rainbow copy of $P_k$. **Johnston, Palmer and Sarkar's conjecture.** For $k\geq 6$, 

$$
\operatorname{ex}^{*}(n,P_k)=\left(\frac{k-1}{2}\right)n+O(1).
$$

This conjecture proposes that the lower bound previously constructed for the rainbow Turán number of every path $P_k$ with $k\geq 6$ is asymptotically sharp up to an additive constant; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Ervin Győri, Ryan R. Martin, Addisu Paulos, Casey Tompkins and Kitti Varga, “On the rainbow planar Turán number of paths”, arXiv:2301.10393 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10393

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: Caro–Petruševski–Škrekovski's proper conflict-free coloring Brooks conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree and $\chi_{\mathrm{pcf}}(G)$ its proper conflict-free chromatic number, the minimum number of colors in a proper coloring in which every vertex of positive degree has a color appearing exactly once on its neighborhood.

**Proper conflict-free coloring Brooks conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta(G)\geq 3,
$$

then

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{pcf}}(G)\leq \Delta(G)+1.
$$

This is a strengthening of odd coloring and was proposed by the originators of the odd coloring conjecture as an additional Brooks-type statement. The supplied source gives no resolution of this conjecture.
record.source_name: Eun-Kyung Cho, Ilkyoo Choi, Hyemin Kwon and Boram Park, “Brooks-type theorems for relaxations of square colorings”, arXiv:2302.06125 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.06125

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: Bang-Jensen–Yeo arc-partition conjecture for highly arc-connected digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph. An **arc-partition** is a partition of its arc set into two parts, $A=A_1\cup A_2$, and a subdigraph is **spanning and strong** if it has vertex set $V$ and is strongly connected.

**Bang-Jensen–Yeo's conjecture.** There exists an integer $K$ such that every $K$-arc-strong digraph $D=(V,A)$ has an arc-partition

$$
A=A_1\cup A_2
$$

such that each of the subdigraphs $D_1=(V,A_1)$ and $D_2=(V,A_2)$ is spanning and strong.

This conjecture would imply Thomassen's good-pair conjecture by decomposing a sufficiently arc-strong digraph into two spanning strong subdigraphs. The source states that it is open; in particular, the minimum such $K$ is unknown.
record.source_name: Joergen Bang-Jensen and Yun Wang, “Arc-disjoint out-branchings and in-branchings in semicomplete digraphs”, arXiv:2302.06177 (2023).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2206.12092](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12092), [arXiv:1812.08809](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.08809), [arXiv:1808.02740](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.02740).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.06177

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: The four-color conjecture for certain degenerate triangles in the max-norm plane
record.statement:
Let $a,b$ be coprime positive integers with $a\not\equiv b\pmod{3}$, and let $T(a,b,a+b)$ be the degenerate triangle with side parameters $a$, $b$, and $a+b$. Write $\chi(\mathbb{R}_\infty^2,T)$ for the minimum number of colors needed to color the max-norm plane so that no $\ell_\infty$-isometric copy of $T$ is monochromatic. **Four-color conjecture.**

$$
\chi\bigl(\mathbb{R}_\infty^2,T(a,b,a+b)\bigr)=4.
$$

In the stated congruence case, three colors are known to be insufficient, and the claim was verified by computer search when $a+b\leq 7$.
record.source_name: Alexander Natalchenko and Arsenii Sagdeev, “Monochromatic triangles in the max-norm plane”, arXiv:2302.09972 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.09972

record.title: You and Liu's Laplacian spectral ratio conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $n\geq 3$ vertices. The Laplacian spectral ratio is

$$
R_L(G)=\frac{\mu_1(G)}{\mu_{n-1}(G)},
$$

where $\mu_1(G)$ and $\mu_{n-1}(G)$ are the largest and second smallest Laplacian eigenvalues of a connected graph $G$. **You and Liu's conjecture.**

$$
R_L(K_{1,\,n-1})\leq R_L(T)\leq R_L(P_n),
$$

and the left equality holds if and only if $T=K_{1,\,n-1}$, while the right equality holds if and only if $T=P_n$. This conjecture proposes that among trees on $n$ vertices the star minimizes and the path maximizes the Laplacian spectral ratio; the source notes that conditions in terms of diameter and maximum degree had been established, but provides no resolution of the full conjecture.
record.source_name: Zhen Lin, Jiajia Wang and Min Cai, “The Laplacian spectral ratio of connected graphs”, arXiv:2302.10491 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.10491

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: Reinhart's normalized distance Laplacian spectral-radius characterization
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\partial_n^\mathcal{L}$ denote the largest eigenvalue of its normalized distance Laplacian matrix $\mathcal{D}^\mathcal{L}(G)$. **Reinhart's conjecture.**

$$
\partial_n^\mathcal{L}=\frac{n}{n-1}
$$

if and only if $G$ is the complete graph $K_n$.

Reinhart proposed this characterization after proving the bound $\partial_n^\mathcal{L}\geq n/(n-1)$ for graphs on at least two vertices. The supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Jacob Johnston and Michael Tait, “Extremal values for the spectral radius of the normalized distance Laplacian”, arXiv:2302.11459 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11459

record.title: The spanning-tree decomposition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $T$ be a spanning tree of $G$, and let $(T,\mathcal{B})$ be a tree decomposition of $G$ with width measured as the maximum bag size minus one. Write $\operatorname{tw}(G)$ for the treewidth of $G$.

**The spanning-tree decomposition conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that every connected graph $G$ has a tree decomposition $(T,\mathcal{B})$ of width at most $f(\operatorname{tw}(G))$ such that $T$ is a spanning tree of $G$.

This is presented as a strengthening of the minor version and is one of three conjectures reduced successively to the next. The supplied text does not state its independent resolution, although the paper's overall strategy ultimately disproves the final, stronger conjecture.
record.source_name: Pablo Blanco, Linda Cook, Meike Hatzel, Claire Hilaire, Freddie Illingworth and Rose McCarty, “On tree decompositions whose trees are minors”, arXiv:2302.12106 (2023).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12106

record.title: Jiang–Polyanskii conjecture on the bounded secondary term for equiangular lines
record.statement:
For $alpha\in(0,1)$, let $\lambda=(1-\alpha)/(2\alpha)$, and let $k(\lambda)$ denote the minimum number of vertices of a graph whose largest eigenvalue is exactly $\lambda$, or $\infty$ if no such graph exists. **Jiang–Polyanskii conjecture.** If $k(\lambda)=\infty$, then

$$
N_\alpha(n)=n+O_\alpha(1).
$$

The quantity $N_\alpha(n)$ concerns the maximum size of a family of equiangular lines with common angle parameter $\alpha$. The conjecture would determine the secondary term in the $k(\lambda)=\infty$ case, strengthening the known estimate $N_\alpha(n)=n+o(n)$; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Carl Schildkraut, “Equiangular lines and large multiplicity of fixed second eigenvalue”, arXiv:2302.12230 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12230

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: Vizing's edge-recoloring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree, and let a proper edge-coloring be a coloring of the edges in which adjacent edges receive different colors. Two edge-colorings are **equivalent** if one can be transformed into the other by a sequence of Kempe swaps.

**Vizing's conjecture.** Every $k$-edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is equivalent to a $\Delta(G)$-edge-coloring of $G$ if there is any.

This conjecture asks whether every edge-coloring can be reconfigured to an optimal edge-coloring whenever one exists. The supplied source does not state whether it is resolved.
record.source_name: Jonathan Narboni, “Vizing's edge-recoloring conjecture holds”, arXiv:2302.12914 (2023).
record.references:
**8 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2005–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2301.02140](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.02140), [arXiv:1909.01260](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.01260), [arXiv:1904.12060](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12060), [arXiv:1805.05996](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.05996), [arXiv:1506.02576](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02576), [arXiv:1401.4568](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.4568), [arXiv:math/0512518](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0512518).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12914

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: The $(\Delta(G)+2)$-edge-coloring equivalence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, and let an edge-coloring be proper when adjacent edges receive different colors. Two edge-colorings are **equivalent** if one can be transformed into the other by a sequence of Kempe swaps.

**The $(\Delta(G)+2)$-edge-coloring equivalence conjecture.** All $(\Delta(G)+2)$-edge-colorings of a graph $G$ are equivalent.

The claim concerns connectivity of the reconfiguration space of edge-colorings under Kempe swaps. The supplied source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Jonathan Narboni, “Vizing's edge-recoloring conjecture holds”, arXiv:2302.12914 (2023).

record.title: The non-optimal edge-coloring equivalence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and call an edge-coloring **optimal** if it uses the minimum possible number of colors. Two edge-colorings are **equivalent** if one can be transformed into the other by a sequence of Kempe swaps; a coloring is **non-optimal** if it is not optimal.

**The non-optimal edge-coloring equivalence conjecture.** Any two non-optimal colorings are equivalent.

This is presented as a consequence of the stronger question asking whether every optimal coloring is equivalent to every given coloring. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture is resolved.
record.source_name: Jonathan Narboni, “Vizing's edge-recoloring conjecture holds”, arXiv:2302.12914 (2023).

record.title: The finite-field sharp exceptional-set conjecture in three dimensions
record.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{F}_p^3$ satisfy

$$
\#A=p^a.
$$

Recall the exceptional set $E_s(A)$ for projection to lines or planes. Let $t(a,s)$ be the lower bound for $T(a,s)$ given by Proposition 1 for projections to lines, or by Proposition 2 for projections to planes. **Finite-field sharp exceptional-set conjecture.** In either case,

$$
\#E_s(A)\leq C_{\epsilon,a,s}p^{\epsilon+t(a,s)}.
$$

This conjecture transfers the proposed sharp Euclidean exponents to projections in $
\mathbb{F}_p^3$ and predicts that the explicit examples determine the exceptional-set size up to an $
\epsilon$-loss. The source does not give evidence of resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Paige Bright and Shengwen Gan, “Exceptional set estimates in finite fields”, arXiv:2302.13193 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13193

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: Multigraph Overfull Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph with no loops, and let $\mu(G)$ be its maximum edge multiplicity. Let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, let $\chi'(G)$ be its chromatic index, and call a subgraph $H$ **$\Delta(G)$-overfull** when $\Delta(H)=\Delta(G)$ and $|E(H)|>\Delta(H)\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$.

**Multigraph Overfull Conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta(G)>\frac{1}{3}\mu(G)|V(G)|,
$$

then $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)$ if and only if $G$ contains no $\Delta(G)$-overfull subgraph.

This is the multigraph analogue of the Overfull Conjecture. The degree condition is shown in the source to be best possible using suitable multigraphs derived from the Petersen graph, but the conjecture itself is not resolved there.
record.source_name: Michael J. Plantholt and Songling Shan, “On the Multigraph Overfull Conjecture”, arXiv:2302.13197 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13197

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: Bonamy et al.'s odd-degree planar edge-partition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph of odd maximum degree $\Delta\ge 7$. A **linear forest** is a forest whose connected components are paths, and a **matching** is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges.

**Odd-degree planar edge-partition conjecture.** The edges of $G$ can be partitioned into $\tfrac{\Delta-1}{2}$ linear forests and one matching.

The conjecture seeks a stronger decomposition than the general linear-arboricity bound in the odd-degree planar case. The paper proves this conclusion for odd maximum degree at least $9$, leaving the cases covered by the stated conjecture below that threshold open.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Jadwiga Czyżewska, Łukasz Kowalik and Michał Pilipczuk, “Partitioning edges of a planar graph into linear forests and a matching”, arXiv:2302.13312 (2023).

record.title: Day's conical-vertex conjecture for extremal $K_r$-saturated graphs
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 4$ and $t\geq r-2$ be integers. Let $C(r,t)$ denote the family of graphs defined by $C(r,t)=C(r,t,-c(r,t))$, where $c(r,t)$ is the corresponding extremal constant for $K_r$-saturated graphs with minimum degree at least $t$. A **conical vertex** is a vertex adjacent to every other vertex. **Day's conjecture.** Every graph in $C(r,t)$ has a conical vertex.

This conjecture is equivalent to the assertion that, for fixed $r\geq 4$ and $t\geq r-2$ and sufficiently large $n$, every extremal graph for $sat(n,K_r,t)$ has a conical vertex. The source reports Day's speculation and states that the author believes it to be true, but provides no resolution.
record.source_name: Asier Calbet, “K_r-saturated Graphs and the Two Families Theorem”, arXiv:2302.13389 (2023).

record.title: Covering gonality bound for Gorenstein unicuspidal rational curves
record.statement:
Let $C$ be a Gorenstein unicuspidal rational curve of genus $g$, and let $\gon_F(C)$ denote its covering gonality, namely the smallest degree of a map from $C$ to $\mathbb{P}^1$. **Covering gonality conjecture.**

$$
\gon_F(C)\leq\left\lceil\frac{g+1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This proposes a uniform upper bound for the covering gonality of Gorenstein unicuspidal rational curves. The supplied text gives no evidence that the bound has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Frank's continuation conjecture for the three-dimensional Bohr–Wheeler branch
record.statement: Let $\chi$ be the fissility parameter. The Bohr–Wheeler branch is the bifurcation branch of three-dimensional saddle points, and a saddle point is the transition state along the corresponding minimum energy path. **Frank's continuation conjecture.** The Bohr–Wheeler branch in three dimensions continues to arbitrarily small $\chi$, and the saddle point on this branch converges to two touching balls as $\chi\to0$. This conjecture is stated in Frank's work and is supported by the paper's numerical results, but the supplied text does not establish it.
record.source_name: Zirui Xu and Qiang Du, “Bifurcation and fission in the liquid drop model: a phase-field approach”, arXiv:2302.14449 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.14449

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2023). “This conjecture remains open, since the proof given by Frank is only valid in a small neighborhood of $\fis=\fis_*$ .”

record.title: Packing version of Dinitz's problem
record.statement:
For an integer $n\geq 3$, let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $K_n\mathbin\square K_n$ denote their Cartesian product, and let $\chi_\ell^\star$ denote the list packing number.

**Packing version of Dinitz's problem.** For $n\geq 3$,

$$
\chi_\ell^\star(K_n\mathbin\square K_n)=n+1.
$$

The graph $K_n\mathbin\square K_n$ is the line graph of $K_{n,n}$, and its ordinary list chromatic number is $n$ by Galvin's theorem, whereas the paper shows that its list packing number exceeds $n$. Determining whether the exact value is $n+1$ remains open.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie, Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Ewan Davies and Ross J. Kang, “List packing number of bounded degree graphs”, arXiv:2303.01246 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.01246

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

record.title: Conjecture on the non-Gorenstein locus of Schubert varieties
record.statement: Let $X_w$ be a Schubert variety, and let $({\mathfrak S},\prec_I)$ be the poset of permutation intervals. The order ideal of intervals corresponding to points where Schubert varieties are not Gorenstein is denoted ${\mathcal I}_{\mathrm{not\ Gorenstein}}$. **Non-Gorenstein locus conjecture.** The order ideal ${\mathcal I}_{\mathrm{not\ Gorenstein}}$ is generated by families (1) and (2) in the stated characterization of Gorenstein Schubert varieties. This would determine the locus of non-Gorenstein points; the supplied text does not state a resolution status.
record.source_name: Alexander Woo and Alexander Yong, “Schubert geometry and combinatorics”, arXiv:2303.01436 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.01436

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2023).

record.title: The diagonal-maximality conjecture for correspondence packing of complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
For positive integers $a$ and $b$ with $a>b$, let $K_{a,b}$ denote the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $a$ and $b$, and let $\chi_c^\star$ denote its correspondence packing number. **Diagonal-maximality conjecture.**

$$
\chi_c^\star(K_{a+1,b})\le \chi_c^\star(K_{a,b+1}).
$$

Thus, among complete bipartite graphs with a fixed total number of vertices, the maximum value is conjectured to occur on the diagonal, in the sense stated above. The source notes that this is analogous to a belief about Ramsey numbers and is also expected for the list and correspondence colouring parameters; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Evans-type conjecture for cartesian products with $K_2$
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $k$ be an integer, and write $G\square K_2$ for the cartesian product of $G$ and the complete graph on two vertices. Write $\chi'(G)$ for the edge-chromatic number of $G$. **Evans-type conjecture for cartesian products with $K_2$.** If every precoloring of at most $k$ edges of $G$ can be extended to a proper $\chi'(G)$-edge coloring, then every precoloring of at most $k+1$ edges of $G\square K_2$ is extendable to a proper $(\chi'(G)+1)$-edge coloring of $G\square K_2$. The paper verifies this conjecture for trees, complete and complete bipartite graphs, and graphs with small maximum degree, while giving partial results for general regular graphs; the general assertion remains open.

record.title: Hilton's conjecture on subgraph-overfull graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $V$ and $E$ denote its vertex and edge sets, and let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree. A graph is **Class 1** if its edges can be properly colored with $\Delta(G)$ colors; otherwise it is Class 2. A graph is **subgraph-overfull** if it has a subgraph $H$ satisfying $|V(H)|$ odd and

$$
|E(H)|>\Delta(G)\frac{|V(H)|-1}{2}.
$$

**Hilton's conjecture.** If $\Delta(G)>\frac{|V|}{3}$, then $G$ is Class 1 if and only if it is not subgraph-overfull.
The supplied paper states that this conjecture holds for the class of split graphs with stretch index $\sigma=2$, but does not establish its general status.
record.source_name: Fernanda Couto, Diego Amaro Ferraz and Sulamita Klein, “New Results on Edge-coloring and Total-coloring of Split Graphs”, arXiv:2303.05723 (2024).

record.title: Figueiredo et al.'s conjecture on chordal graph edge-coloring
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a chordal graph, meaning a graph with no induced cycle of length at least $4$. Let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree. A graph is **Class 2** if its edges cannot be properly colored with $\Delta(G)$ colors, and it is **subgraph-overfull** if it has a subgraph $H$ satisfying $|V(H)|$ odd and

$$
|E(H)|>\Delta(G)\frac{|V(H)|-1}{2}.
$$

**Figueiredo et al.'s conjecture.** $G$ is Class 2 if and only if it is subgraph-overfull.
This conjecture proposes a characterization of edge-chromatic Class 2 chordal graphs by the subgraph-overfull obstruction. The supplied text gives no resolution beyond noting that the paper's results cover a class of split graphs.

record.title: Infinite counterexample conjecture for Seifert-fibre edges
record.statement:
A **small Seifert fibre space** is a Seifert fibre space containing no embedded two-sided incompressible surfaces. A **one-vertex triangulation** has exactly one vertex, and an edge is **isotopic to a Seifert fibre** when the embedded curve it realizes is isotopic to a circle fibre. A **prism manifold** is the class excluded in the statement, alongside lens spaces.

**Infinite Seifert-fibre counterexample conjecture.** For every small Seifert fibre space that is not a lens space or prism manifold, there exist infinitely many one-vertex triangulations with no edges isotopic to Seifert fibres.

The paper proves the analogous conclusion for two specific small Seifert fibre spaces and reports failed searches for several others. The general statement is proposed as an unanswered question and is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Scalar-flatness conjecture for complete critical metrics of the scalar-curvature functional
record.statement:
Let $(M^{n},g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\geq5$. Write

$$
\mathfrak{S}^{2}=\int R_g^{2}\,dV_g
$$

for the quadratic scalar-curvature functional. A critical metric has **finite energy** when this integral is finite.

**Scalar-flatness conjecture.** If $(M^{n},g)$ is a complete critical metric of $\mathfrak{S}^{2}$ with finite energy, then $(M^{n},g)$ is scalar flat, and hence is a global minimum of $\mathfrak{S}^{2}$.

This conjecture asserts that the lower-bound hypothesis on the scalar curvature can be removed from the previously known scalar-flatness result in dimensions $n\geq5$. The source does not state a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: Calta–Kraaikamp–Schmidt natural-extension conjecture for triangle-group continued fractions
record.statement:
For each integer $n\geq 3$ and parameter $\alpha\in(0,1)$, let $T_{n,\alpha}$ be the continued fraction map associated with the triangle Fuchsian group $G_n$, and let its first pointwise expansive power be the first iterate that is pointwise expansive. A natural extension is an invertible measure-preserving system projecting onto the original system.

**Calta–Kraaikamp–Schmidt conjecture.** For all $n\geq 3$ and all $\alpha\in(0,1)$, the natural extension of the first pointwise expansive power of $T_{n,\alpha}$ is given by the first return of the geodesic flow to a cross section in the unit tangent bundle of the hyperbolic orbifold uniformized by $G_n$.

The conjecture connects these continued fraction transformations with geodesic-flow codings. The paper proves the relevant entropy and natural-extension results and establishes an equivalent volume identity, but the asserted identification is presented as conjectural.

record.title: Quantitative max-sum matching conjecture for diametral balls
record.statement: Let $d$ be a positive integer. Let $X$ be an even set of distinct points in $\mathbb R^d$ with minimum distance $r>0$, and let $\mathcal M$ be a max-sum matching of $X$. The closed balls induced by $\mathcal M$ are the balls having the matched pairs as diameters. **Quantitative max-sum matching conjecture.** There exists a constant $\varepsilon_d>0$ such that the intersection of the closed balls induced by $\mathcal M$ contains a ball of radius $\varepsilon_d r$. This is a quantitative strengthening of the question of whether every max-sum matching is an open Tverberg graph. The corresponding qualitative problem is known affirmatively in dimension $2$ but remains open in general dimensions, and the quantitative assertion is posed as a conjecture.

record.title: Chappell–Pelsmajer's induced subgraph conjecture for bounded-treewidth graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ and treewidth at most $k$, where $k\geq 0$. An induced subgraph $G[S]$ has maximum degree at most $1$ if every vertex in $S$ is adjacent to at most one other vertex in $S$. **Chappell–Pelsmajer's conjecture.** Every such graph admits a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that

$$
|S|\geq\left\lceil\frac{2n}{k+2}\right\rceil.
$$

This extends the bound they proved for $k\leq 3$ to all nonnegative values of $k$; the paper presents it as a conjecture and does not provide a resolution.

record.title: One-third conjecture for clustered sets in planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $S\subseteq V(G)$. Write $\alpha_{\mathcal{P},2}(G)$ for the maximum size of a set $S$ whose induced subgraph has maximum degree at most $1$, equivalently, such that every vertex in $S$ is adjacent to at most one other vertex in $S$. **One-third conjecture for planar graphs.** Every planar graph has such a set $S$ containing at least one third of its vertices; equivalently,

$$
\alpha_{\mathcal{P},2}(G)=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

The octahedron gives the matching upper bound, so the conjecture asserts that this bound is best possible. It is implied by the Albertson–Berman conjecture that every planar graph has an induced forest on at least half of its vertices, but neither conjecture is resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Weighted logarithmic mean characterisation of harmonic functions
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^m$, with $m\geqslant 2$. Let $A_x(r_1,r_2)$ be an admissible annular domain centred at $x$, with $r_2>r_1>0$, and let $B_{r_2}(x)$ be admissible. Denote by $M^\circ(S_r(x),u)$ the spherical mean of $u$ over $S_r(x)$, and let $r$ either attain each value in $(r_1,r_2)$ or equal $r_i$ for $i=1$ or $2$. **Weighted logarithmic mean conjecture.** If $u\in C^0(D)$ satisfies, for every $x\in D$ and every such $A_x(r_1,r_2)$,

$$
\frac{m}{|A(r_1,r_2)|}\int_{A_x(r_1,r_2)}u(y)\log\frac{r}{|x-y|}\,\mathrm{d}y=M^\circ(S_r(x),u),
$$

then $u$ is harmonic in $D$. The identity extends the logarithmic weighted mean property of harmonic functions from balls to annular domains; the stated result is presented after the corresponding harmonic characterisations and its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Nikolay Kuznetsov, “A characterisation of harmonic functions by quadrature identities of annular domains and related results”, arXiv:2303.15408 (2023).

record.title: Density threshold for typical Hodge loci in the Torelli locus
record.statement: Let $g\geqslant4$ be an integer, let $S\subset\mathcal A_g$ be a closed Hodge generic subvariety of dimension $q$, and let $\mathbb V$ be the induced polarizable $\mathbb Z$-VHS on $S$. The **Torelli-locus typical-density conjecture.** The typical Hodge locus of $S$ for $\mathbb V$ is analytically dense if and only if $q\geqslant g-1$. When this holds, the Hecke translates of $\mathcal A_{g-1}\times\mathcal A_1$ in $\mathcal A_g$ intersect $S$ in an analytically dense subset. This predicts the precise dimension threshold for density in the Siegel modular variety and identifies the largest relevant strict special subvarieties.
